pool.text: During a calculus diagnostic assessment, A wildlife population \(P(t)\) follows the logistic differential equation \(\dfrac{dP}{dt} = \frac{1}{2}P\left(1 - \dfrac{P}{200}\right)\) with \(P(0) = 50\), illustrated qualitatively by the logistic slope field shown.
pool.educational_aim: Approximate solutions of initial-value problems with Euler's method and analyze logistic differential equations and slope fields.
pool.exam_archetype: Euler's Method & Logistic Differential Equations
pool.sol: (a) Fastest growth occurs at \(P = \frac{M}{2} = 100\), where \(\left.\frac{dP}{dt}\right|_{\max} = \frac{1}{2}(100)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 25\). (b) Step 1: \(y(0.5) \approx 1 + 0.5(0 + 1) = \frac{3}{2}\); Step 2: \(y(1) \approx \frac{3}{2} + 0.5(0.5 + \frac{3}{2}) = \frac{5}{2}\).
hints: A logistic curve \(\frac{dP}{dt} = kP(1 - P/M)\) has its inflection point at \(P = M/2\).
Update \(y_{n+1} = y_n + \Delta x (x_n + y_n)\) twice from \(x_0 = 0\) to \(x_2 = 1\).

pool.text: A culture's population \(P(t)\), modeled by the logistic slope field shown, satisfies \(\dfrac{dP}{dt} = 2P - \dfrac{2}{40}P^2\) with \(P(0) = 20\). What is \(\lim_{t \to \infty} P(t)\)?
pool.educational_aim: Approximate solutions of initial-value problems with Euler's method and analyze logistic differential equations and slope fields.
pool.exam_archetype: Euler's Method & Logistic Differential Equations
pool.sol: Factor \(\frac{dP}{dt} = 2P\left(1 - \frac{P}{40}\right)\). The carrying capacity is \(M = 40\), so for \(P(0) = 20 > 0\), \(\lim_{t\to\infty} P(t) = 40\).
hints: Factor \(2P\) out of \(2P - \frac{2}{40}P^2\) to put the ODE in standard logistic form \(kP(1 - P/M)\).
Identify the carrying capacity \(M\) where \(\frac{dP}{dt} = 0\) for \(P > 0\).
Any positive initial condition \(P(0) > 0\) approaches \(M\) as \(t \to \infty\).

figure.title: Slope Field for Autonomous Logistic Model (M = 40)

pool.sympy_cert: P = sp.Symbol('P', positive=True); EXPECTED = sp.solve(2*P - sp.Rational(2, 40)*P**2, P)[0]

pool.text: Determine the exact result for the following setup: Find the slope \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) of the line tangent to the polar limaçon \(r(\theta) = 4 + 1\cos\theta\) at \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\).

pool.exam_archetype: Power Series, Taylor Polynomials & Lagrange Error
pool.sol: By the Ratio Test, \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \left|\frac{(x-(2))^{n+1}}{4^{n+1}(n+1)^2} \cdot \frac{4^n n^2}{(x-(2))^n}\right| = \frac{|x - (2)|}{4} < 1 \implies R = 4\).
hints: Remember the radius \(R\) is half the length of the convergence interval.

pool.text: A particle traces the polar curve \(r(\theta) = 3 + 2\sin\theta\). Find \(\left.\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}\right|_{\theta = \pi/2}\).
pool.educational_aim: Synthesize BC calculus techniques across multi-part Taylor series, polar/parametric motion, Euler/logistic, and tabular integration problems.
pool.exam_archetype: AP Calculus BC Multi-Part Section II Synthesis
pool.sol: Since \(x(\theta) = r(\theta)\cos\theta\), \(\frac{dx}{d\theta} = r'(\theta)\cos\theta - r(\theta)\sin\theta\). At \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}\), \(\cos(\pi/2)=0\) and \(r(\pi/2) = 5\), so \(\frac{dx}{d\theta} = -5\).
hints: Express the Cartesian coordinate as \(x(\theta) = r(\theta)\cos\theta\).
Differentiate using the Product Rule: \(x'(\theta) = r'(\theta)\cos\theta - r(\theta)\sin\theta\).
pool.sympy_cert: th = sp.Symbol('th'); EXPECTED = sp.diff((3 + 2*sp.sin(th))*sp.cos(th), th).subs(th, sp.pi/2)

pool.text: For the system described below, A particle traces the polar curve \(r(\theta) = 4 + 4\sin\theta\). Find \(\left.\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}\right|_{\theta = \pi/2}\).
pool.educational_aim: Synthesize BC calculus techniques across multi-part Taylor series, polar/parametric motion, Euler/logistic, and tabular integration problems.
pool.exam_archetype: AP Calculus BC Multi-Part Section II Synthesis
pool.sol: Since \(x(\theta) = r(\theta)\cos\theta\), \(\frac{dx}{d\theta} = r'(\theta)\cos\theta - r(\theta)\sin\theta\). At \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}\), \(\cos(\pi/2)=0\) and \(r(\pi/2) = 8\), so \(\frac{dx}{d\theta} = -8\).
hints: Express the Cartesian coordinate as \(x(\theta) = r(\theta)\cos\theta\).
Differentiate using the Product Rule: \(x'(\theta) = r'(\theta)\cos\theta - r(\theta)\sin\theta\).
pool.sympy_cert: th = sp.Symbol('th'); EXPECTED = sp.diff((4 + 4*sp.sin(th))*sp.cos(th), th).subs(th, sp.pi/2)
